subject: Multi-cloud marketplace: SKU availability mapping + canary packaging
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-cloud marketplace: SKU availability mapping + canary packaging

Team —

Following up from last week's partner sync: Nimbus Analytics (the prospect) asked us to list a minimal set of SKUs on AWS/Azure/GCP to support a phased co-sell plan across US regions. The partners want: a) clear SKU names that map to our Dedicated/Private/Hosted tiers, b) region availability per cloud (start with core US regions, then expand), and c) a lightweight "canary" package we can list first to unblock sales while we work on full regional coverage.

Key constraints we heard from partners:
- AWS: prefer 3 canonical SKUs (dev, standard, enterprise) with BYOL options; initial regions: us-east-1, us-west-2.
- Azure: single SKU per tier but explicit VM/size mapping required; start: eastus, westus2.
- GCP: they want a single containerized listing tied to a managed marketplace SKU; start: us-central1.

Attached: SKU-availability-matrix.xlsx (first pass) and canary-pack-readme.md with suggested canary contents.

Asks:
1) Karthik — validate the canary technical constraints (image size, latency SLA offsets for the smaller package).
2) Ben — propose the go-to-market naming and co-sell commitment language (what we promise in the first 90 days).
3) Laura — run legal/partner ops check on the BYOL wording and any marketplace-specific T&Cs.

Goal: agree on a minimal marketable SKU set by EOD Wed so I can get the listings into partners' staging portals and schedule the canary launch for next Tuesday (4/20).

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Head of Partner GTM | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SKU-availability-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 42KB)]
[Attachment: canary-pack-readme.md (md, 6KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud marketplace: SKU availability mapping + canary packaging

Tessa —

Quick technical read: the canary package as outlined in the readme is feasible but with a few caveats:
- Image size: we should keep the container under 3.5GB to satisfy partner cold-start limits on Marketplace. Current build is ~5GB; I'll strip debug symbols and split optional components.
- KV cache warmup: canary should include a small KV snapshot to avoid first-token latency > 600ms in us-east-1; I can bake a minimal prefix cache for the canary.
- Quantization/FP: for the canary we'll ship an int8 variant only on AWS and GCP; Azure needs a separate S45-compatible bundle (their marketplace validation flagged FP16 artifacts).

Region mapping: start with the three canonical regions you listed, but add oregon (us-west-2) for continuity on AWS — we already have infra there for Dedicated customers.

I will update SKU-availability-matrix.xlsx with technical flags (image-size, kv-required, quantization-profile) by EOD today.

- Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dominic Reyes <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>, Priya Nambiar <azure-marketplace@microsoft.com>, Mateo Silva <gcp-partner@google.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud marketplace: SKU availability mapping + canary packaging

Looping in partner contacts so we don't jump ahead on naming/offer text. Short thoughts on GTM/naming:

- SKU naming: keep it simple and cloud-neutral: Redwood Inference • Starter, Redwood Inference • Scale, Redwood Inference • Enterprise. Partners prefer the cloud-agnostic label up front.
- Canary package: call it "Starter (Canary)" and explicitly list limits: 4 vCPU equivalent, 32GB memory, 1 concurrent instance per customer in marketplace listings (helps manage capacity).
- Co-sell commitment: for the canary, we offer 30-day onboarding support and a joint demand gen credit of $5k for qualified pipeline we bring to the partner listing (partners: confirm this is acceptable).

Dominic/Priya/Mateo — can you confirm partner-side constraints on the co-sell credit language and whether AWS/GCP require Marketplace contracts for the $5k credit to be handled as partner rebates vs. listing text?

If partners approve, let's lock the SKU names and I'll draft the marketplace copy for each cloud (short blurb + 3 bullet features + support SLA) and circulate for legal.

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Cloud GTM | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: aws-pricing-diff.csv (csv, 3KB)]

From: Dominic Reyes <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Priya Nambiar <azure-marketplace@microsoft.com>, Mateo Silva <gcp-partner@google.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-cloud marketplace: SKU availability mapping + canary packaging

Ben/Tessa —

AWS side: the naming convention is fine. A couple of notes:
- The $5k co-sell credit needs to be handled via a partner rebate (we can't surface it as direct listing text). We'll work with your partner ops to set up a rebate code.
- Lists with BYOL options are OK but we require a clear customer flow on the listing; recommend a short bullet "Bring your own model license (BYOL) — contact support for license activation".
- Regarding regions: us-east-1 + us-west-2 is a good starting set for the canary. If you can provide the smaller image and the KV snapshot we'll validate in staging this week.

I'll assign an onboarding rep once the final artifacts are uploaded to our portal.

— Dominic
AWS Marketplace Partner Manager
[Inbound: please attach the staging bundle to the shared Drive link and cc marketplace-onboard@amazon.com]
